title: What Is Advance Ship Notice Inbound Signal Accuracy?
summary: An ASN marked "shipped" doesn't mean a full truck arrives on time. See why ASN accuracy protects production schedules and procurement's credibility with the plant.

# What Is Advance Ship Notice Inbound Signal Accuracy?


By[Jacqueline Nance](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/profile/jacqueline-nance) , *Sr. Content Marketing Manager*


Last Updated September 21, 2026


6 min read


In this article, learn about:


-


What "shipped" actually means on an ASN, and why a supplier's system can report it accurately and still be wrong


-


Why a false positive ASN becomes procurement's problem to explain, even though supply chain feels the consequence


-


What real inbound shipment visibility requires beyond a faster dashboard


---


In the system, the shipment looked right. The advance ship notice (ASN) showed it leaving on time and in full. Yet by the time it reached the receiving door, the physical shipment told a different story: a partial pallet, the wrong lot, or a truck that had left a day late.


That gap between what the system records and what moves through the supply chain is where small discrepancies can become larger operational problems.


ASN accuracy is supposed to be the source of truth document that a team can plan around before a truck ever arrives. When that fact turns out to be wrong, procurement is the team explaining to operations why a schedule built on a confirmed shipment just came apart.


## What Does Shipped Actually Mean on an ASN?


An ASN records what a supplier's system believes happened at the dock, not necessarily what a receiving team will find when the truck opens. Most ASNs are generated the moment an order is picked or invoiced, sometimes before a single case is loaded. The document says shipped. The transaction that would confirm it, an actual load, a carrier pickup, a scan at the door, may still be hours or days away. A manufacturing plant scheduling a production run around that ASN is scheduling around an intention.


**Related Reading:**[EDI 856: Advance Ship Notice/Manifest](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-856-ship-notice-manifest)


## Why This Problem Lands on Procurement's Desk


Whereas supply chain owns the consequence when a line stops, procurement owns the supplier relationship that produced the bad signal in the first place. That split puts procurement in an uncomfortable spot: the team gets the escalation after the fact, with little visibility into which suppliers are generating false positives and which are simply slow.


The pattern typically shows up before any single shipment goes wrong. A supplier's ASN accuracy rate is a leading indicator of how much manual verification their transactions require, and manual verification is expensive. Every ASN that has to be double-checked against a phone call or a portal login pulls a buyer or planner away from work that actually needs their judgment. Multiply that across a supplier base of any size and the costs can become staggering, looking more a structural problem than an occasional headache.


## The False Positive ASN Problem Is a Timing Problem


It's tempting to treat a false positive ASN as a supplier training issue: get them to enter better data and the problem goes away. That misses what is actually happening.


Most false positives come from a mismatch between when a supplier's system fires the ASN and when the physical event it describes actually occurs. Fixing that requires the ASN to be tied to something verifiable, a carrier pickup scan, a warehouse confirmation, a shipment status that updates automatically rather than one a person keys in from memory.


A supplier can be well-intentioned and still generate unreliable ASNs if their system has no way to confirm the event before reporting it. The fix is a connection that ties the ASN to the physical reality of the shipment, so the document updates when the truck moves instead of when someone assumes it will.


## What Great Inbound Shipment Visibility Requires


Real inbound shipment visibility means a planner can look at an ASN and trust it enough to act on it without a second call. That requires three things working together:


-


The ASN has to arrive early enough to matter


-


It has to match what physically happens at the dock


-


Any correction has to reach the people who already built a plan around the old version


Most visibility tools solve the first problem and stop there. A dashboard that shows an ASN the moment it's created doesn't tell a planner whether that ASN is trustworthy. Speed without reliability just means the team finds out about the wrong information faster. The gap between seeing a shipment update and being able to act on it without checking it first is exactly where production schedules and procurement's credibility with the plant both take the hit.


## Turning ASN Accuracy Into a Supplier Accountability Conversation


For procurement, ASN accuracy is a performance conversation waiting to happen, if the data exists to have it. Right now, most teams can tell you which suppliers are late. But few can tell you which suppliers are unreliable in a way that shows up as false positives rather than outright delays, because nobody is tracking ASN accuracy as its own metric.


That's a gap worth closing. A supplier scorecard that includes ASN match rate, not just on-time delivery, gives procurement a specific, defensible reason to have the conversation before the next line stop instead of after it. It also gives supply chain a reason to trust procurement's read on a supplier relationship, because the data is there to back it up.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What causes a false positive ASN?


Most false positive ASNs happen because a supplier's system generates the shipment notice at order processing or invoicing, before the physical shipment is confirmed. The document reflects an expectation, not a completed event.


### How is ASN accuracy different from on-time delivery?


On-time delivery measures whether a shipment arrived when promised. ASN accuracy measures whether the advance notice matched what physically arrived, including quantity, item, and timing. A supplier can be on time and still send unreliable ASNs.


### Why does ASN accuracy matter more as manufacturers automate planning?


Automated planning and scheduling systems that use AI to help teams decide faster still depend on the data feeding them. Faster analysis of an inaccurate ASN still produces a bad plan. Improving ASN accuracy protects the value of every system built to act on it.


## Where to Start


Pick one supplier or one material where a false positive ASN has caused real disruption, a missed production run, an expedited freight bill, an uncomfortable conversation with operations.


Ask two questions: how often does that supplier's ASN match what actually arrives, and how much manual checking does your team do because the answer to that question isn't already clear?
